Example 2.5

Find the value of k so that the function can serve as a probability function of the random variable Y

p(y)=\left\{\begin{matrix}ky, & y=1,2,3,4,5\\ 0 & \textit{otherwise}\end{matrix}\right\}. Also find (i) P(Y=5) (ii) P(Y>3)

Solution:

As we know that

\sum_{y=1}^{5}p(y)=1

\sum_{y=1}^{5}ky=1

k\sum_{y=1}^{5}y=1

k[1+2+3+4+5]=1

k(15)=1\quad\Rightarrow k=\frac{1}{15}

Put value of k in the given function we get

$p(y)=\left\{\begin{matrix}\frac{1}{15}y, & y=1,2,3,4,5\\ 0 & \textit{otherwise}\end{matrix}\right\}$

(i) Putting Y = 5 in the formula, we have P(Y=5)=\frac{5}{15}

$(ii)\quad P(Y>3)=P(Y=4)+P(Y=5)=\frac{4}{15}+\frac{5}{15}=\frac{9}{15}$
